primary_source_search.primary_source_identified: COGAT (מתפ"ש) internal crossing data passed to Haaretz, described as 'UN-approved'; not publicly released. COGAT's public dashboard gaza-aid-data.gov.il has been stale since the Oct 2025 ceasefire (per Next Century Foundation index, Oct 2026, and AP Dec 2025).

sources.name: Reuters via Al-Monitor, 15 Oct 2026
sources.finding: Commitment: minimum 600 trucks/day under US-mediated deal; diplomats: 'far fewer than 600' normally enter; COGAT itself said merchant boycott would cut total (humanitarian+commercial) to ~300/day.

sources.name: COGAT public statements (via Yahoo/JPost/Asianet), Dec 2025-Feb 2026
sources.finding: COGAT reported ~4,200 trucks/week consistently through late Feb 2026 — consistent with Haaretz's 'Jan-Feb met the commitment'.

sources.name: Al-Monitor/WFP/OCHA/New Arab, Mar 2026
sources.finding: All crossings closed 28 Feb 2026 (Iran war); Kerem Shalom gradually reopened 3 Mar; ~80% drop in first half of March — directionally corroborates the March low (~4,700).

sources.name: AP analysis of COGAT figures, Dec 2025
sources.finding: Precedent: ~459 trucks/day Oct 12-Dec 7 2025 vs 600 commitment; COGAT refused raw data.

sources.name: UN2720 / OCHA
sources.finding: 2026 monthly truck totals not located; UN reports in pallets (e.g. <42,000 pallets in June vs ~46,600 in May 2026) — not comparable to truck counts.

verified_figures.commitment: 600 trucks/day = 4,200/week; 4,200*52/12 = 18,200/month (arithmetic checks out; lede rounds to ~18,000)
verified_figures.article_monthly_sum_mar_to_mid_nov: ~75,100 (sum of monthly figures) vs ~75,350 (sum of by-origin breakdown) — internally consistent
verified_figures.monthly_share: Mar 26%, Apr 29%, May 53%, Jun 66%, Jul 55%, Aug 55%, Sep 71%, Oct 36%; mid-Nov ~4,000 vs ~9,100 pro-rata = ~44%

body_fetch.method: WebFetch (summarizing fetcher; short verbatim quotes extracted for key sentences)
body_fetch.note: Body visible (paywall notices only on print/Zen views). Fetcher would not return full verbatim text; figures taken from its extraction, key sentences quoted verbatim.

claims.claim_text: Headline: data Israel itself transferred prove it is far from the aid threshold it committed to
claims.verified_figure: Article's own COGAT-sourced figures: Mar-Oct 2026 average ~49% of the 18,200/month threshold; COGAT's own Oct 2026 public statement (~300/day total) also far below 600/day
claims.note: Holds for Mar–mid-Nov 2026 on the article's data and is independently supported by COGAT's public October statement. Caveat: COGAT says the data 'אינם מדויקים' while not publishing alternative figures; Jan–Feb did meet the threshold (article says so).

claims.claim_text: The agreement sets 4,200 trucks with aid and goods per week (600/day), ~18,200 per month
claims.verified_figure: 600/day minimum under US-mediated Oct 2025 deal (Reuters, Oct 2026); 4,200/week is COGAT's own reporting unit; 4,200×52/12=18,200
claims.note: Small definitional caveat: Reuters describes the floor as 600 trucks of humanitarian aid; Haaretz counts aid+commercial against it, which, if anything, flatters Israel's compliance, so the gap is not inflated.

claims.claim_text: In January and February 2026 entries met the commitment
claims.verified_figure: COGAT publicly reported ~4,200 trucks/week consistently through 25 Feb 2026
claims.note: Corroborated by COGAT's own public statements (not independently verified by UN).

claims.verified_figure: No public monthly total located. Directional corroboration: all crossings closed 28 Feb 2026 (Iran war), ~80% drop in first half of March (OCHA/WFP/Save the Children)
claims.note: Exact figures come from COGAT data given only to Haaretz; COGAT's public dashboard is stale. March low is consistent with documented closures.

claims.claim_text: May >9,600; June >12,000; July and August ~10,000 each; September record >13,000
claims.verified_figure: No public COGAT or UN2720 monthly truck totals for 2026 found; UN reports pallets (May ~46,600, June <42,000), not trucks
claims.note: UN's May→June pallet decline does not match Haaretz's May→June truck rise, but units/scope (UN-network aid vs all trucks incl. commercial) differ, so not a contradiction.

claims.verified_figure: COGAT public statement 15 Oct 2026: merchant boycott cuts total to ~300/day; diplomats: 'far fewer than 600' normally
claims.note: Exact totals unverifiable, but COGAT's own public statement directionally supports a low October (6,500/31 ≈ 210/day).

claims.claim_text: In most months since March the number of trucks was about half the threshold or less
claims.verified_figure: On the article's own figures: 3 of 8 months clearly below half (26%, 29%, 36%), 3 at ~53–55%, 2 well above (66%, 71%); Mar–Oct average ~49%
claims.note: Internally consistent arithmetic; 'about half' covers 53–55%. June and September are exceptions the article itself lists.

claims.claim_text: Truck origins since March: Israel ~48,769, Egypt ~13,592, maritime corridor ~7,183, Jordan ~3,462, West Bank ~2,344
claims.verified_figure: No public breakdown located; sum ~75,350 matches article's monthly sum (~75,100)
claims.note: Internally consistent; primary dataset not public.

note: Primary dataset (COGAT figures shared with Haaretz) is unpublished; threshold, Jan–Feb compliance, March collapse and low October are corroborated by public COGAT statements and UN/Reuters reporting. Context items (13 authorized merchants, 36 disqualified NGOs, dual-use restrictions, 70–80% food share, Egyptian trucks ~1/5) were not judged: they are context, not the data-vs-commitment claim this audit covers.
